topic: Warp: An Agentic Development Environment Born Out of the Terminal

key_points: Warp went the opposite way from most AI tools: started as a Rust terminal, expanded outward into an ADE with four pillars — Code, Agents, Terminal, Drive
As of April 2026: 700,000+ active developers, $73M+ funding, 75.8% SWE-bench Verified with GPT-5, #1 on Terminal-Bench at 52%
Full Terminal Use lets agents run commands, interpret output, react to errors just as a human would; 96%+ acceptance of agent-suggested diffs
Oz launched Feb 10 2026 as cloud agent orchestration: triggers (Slack @Oz, GitHub PR, Linear, CI, cron), hundreds of parallel agents, Docker envs, multi-repo
Warp Drive stores Workflows, Notebooks, Prompts, Env Vars, Rules, MCP configs; syncs real-time and becomes agent context
Comparison table: Warp terminal-first ADE vs Cursor VS Code fork vs Claude Code headless terminal agent; SWE-bench 75.8% vs ~79.6% (Sonnet 4.6)
/plan command produces spec-driven plan before execution; AGENTS.md / WARP.md project rules
Warp agents run in two modes: Pair (interactive in current session) and Dispatch (autonomous, notifies when done) with a management UI
Warp reports 96%+ acceptance of agent-suggested diffs — reflects both diff UX and output quality
Key differentiator: Full Terminal Use lets agents run shell commands natively — 'set up staging, run tests, open a PR if tests pass' handled without external tools
Multi-agent threading lets you run multiple independent tasks simultaneously in split panes
82/100 Chiri Score, 36 claims verified, 26 sources checked (Jul 4 2026); founded 2020 by Zach Lloyd (ex-Google Sheets lead), 44 employees, $75.1M Series B
Rust-based GPU-accelerated terminal for macOS/Linux/Windows; block-based output, smart completions (fig specs), command correction, Vim keybindings
Positioning: 'Agentic Development Environment' — distinct from IDEs (VS Code) and CLI agents (Claude Code); terminal's low-level access a natural agent foundation
Oz operates in local-agent (in-app interactive) and cloud-agent modes (background, triggers, schedules, parallelism, observability); multi-model
Universal Agent Support hosts external CLI agents (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, OpenCode): vertical tabs, tab configs, unified notifications, native code review, remote control
Zero Data Retention agreements with Anthropic, OpenAI, Google — no training on customer data; SOC 2 Type II; >56% of Fortune 500 adoption
Pricing: Free $0, Build $20/mo (1,500 credits), Max ~$200/mo, Business ~$50/user, Enterprise custom
Description evolution: 2023 'terminal for the 21st century' → 2025 'terminal reimagined with AI' → 2026 'agentic development environment built around the terminal'
Went open-source April 2026: OpenRank 112.91 (May 2026), 250 active contributors, climbed 42 positions — fastest climber in Top 40
Thesis: coding agents don't need IDEs, they need a shell — command → output → next command feedback loop is native to terminals
Terminal is right surface because: transparency (every action visible), intervention (Ctrl+C), multi-agent (separate sessions), integration (no adapter layer)
'Window manager for coding agents' — doesn't compete with agents, provides the surface where they all run
Honest caveat: watching 3+ agents is cognitively expensive; practical sweet spot is 2 agents under active supervision + 1 fire-and-forget
Open Agentic Development model: even non-technical users shape production tools while agents implement and ship in the open
Open source May 2026, AGPL-3.0 client codebase on GitHub; 37,000+ stars within days, #2 on GitHub trending; 700,000+ developers
BlockList abstraction doesn't care what's inside a block (agent conversation UIs, reasoning steps, code diffs coexist with terminal output)
Performance: SumTree data structure for O(log n) viewport lookups; two-level virtualized rendering
Auto-detects CLI agents and enhances UI — Claude Code shows structured blocks; MCP auto-discovered from ~/.claude.json, .mcp.json, .codex/config.toml (shared server set)
Run Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI all inside Warp; supports bash, fish, zsh, PowerShell

stats.fact: Warp users launch almost 2 million agents per day, usage growing 200% month-over-month
Developers wrote nearly 100 million lines of code per week with Warp, growing 55% week-over-week, against 2+ million codebases synced daily
Warp revenue grew 15x since start of year, with 100% growth in the most recent month
#1 overall coding agent on Terminal-Bench (52%, 20 points ahead of Claude Code) and top-5 on SWE-bench Verified (71%) at launch
Warp surpassed one million active developers in March 2026 and launched Oz, its cloud agent orchestration platform
Warp open-sourced its core product April 28, 2026 under AGPL-3.0 (UI crates MIT); OpenAI was the flagship sponsor; ~37K GitHub stars within days
Founded June 2020 by Zach Lloyd (ex-Google principal engineer, led Google Sheets); ~$73-75.1M raised across Seed/Series A/Series B backed by GV, Sequoia, Sam Altman, Marc Benioff, Dylan Field
Full Terminal Use introduced November 2025 (Agents 3.0) — the only product on the market with it; lets agents operate interactive CLI apps (psql, vim, gdb, top)
Warp adopted by over half of the Fortune 500 and companies including Docker, Ramp, Peloton, OpenAI, Atlassian, Cisco, Netflix, Salesforce

angles: Terminal-first third path: most tools start as editors (Cursor/IDE) or headless CLIs (Claude Code); Warp started as a terminal that expanded outward into a full ADE
Full Terminal Use as the market differentiator — agents operate interactive apps (REPLs, debuggers, servers) that IDE-based agents cannot touch
The terminal is the agent's native home: command → output → next-command feedback loops, transparency, instant Ctrl+C intervention, no adapter layer
Universal Agent Support: Warp as 'window manager' that runs Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, OpenCode in parallel — it competes with iTerm, not with coding agents
Open Agentic Development: open-sourcing April 2026 + OpenAI sponsor — community shapes production tools while agents implement; 'building Warp with Warp' (1M+ line Rust codebase)
Oz cloud orchestration: from local agents to scheduled cloud agent fleets triggered by Slack/GitHub/Linear/CI/cron — the leap past laptop-bound agents
The cognitive-attention caveat: multi-agent isn't free parallelism — supervising 3+ agents degrades quality; 2 supervised + 1 fire-and-forget is the practical sweet spot
Warp as a genuine competitor to Cursor and Claude Code for terminal-heavy infra/backend/DevOps work while keeping the best terminal UX
